findings.claim: The plan's concentration rule, applied to this population, makes decision eligibility unreachable by construction and identity eligibility very likely so. 37 of the 38 counted decision documents are in the review_signal stratum. score_bcr.concentration marks a field concentrated when one stratum's net gain exceeds half the total, so any positive decision gain not carried by F072 alone fails the rule.
findings.evidence: My recount from R32-LABELS-REVIEWED-1.json gives identity 57 / revision 38 / decision 38, excluded F069 / F019. Strata from FROZEN-SELECTION: decision review_signal 37, other 1 (F072). Identity: review_signal 36, drawing 16, other 5, but 37 of 38 decision documents carry identity and the run set takes decision documents first (up to 16). Revision: 29 of 38 decision documents carry it; the 9 revision-only documents are drawing 8, other 1 (26687 7, 15744 2). The rule is in plan v2 section 5.5, DRAFT-DECLARATION.v2 l.217 and score_bcr.py l.198-209 (conc = net>0 and max(by_s) > net/2), which feeds reasons_not_eligible (l.263). By project, decision documents split 27331 12 / 3563 11 / 29255 10 / 26687 3 / 22349 2 / 15744 0 (largest 31.6%), so the project leg has no structural problem.
findings.required_action: Before the declaration: the owner and an independent review decide whether the stratum leg applies to fields whose run-set population comes from one stratum by design. Options: drop or redefine it for decision and identity, or record that decision eligibility cannot be shown on this cohort. Freeze the choice in the declaration. Without this, the budget buys a run whose decision outcome is predetermined.
